title: Valuing One Month of the Opening Billing Span on a Medicare Supplement Policy
content:
When premium is returned on a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies, the value of a single month of the span in which the supplement took effect is settled from the charges standing on that policy's premium account.

**Where the charge posted for the opening span covers more than one month of cover** — a month is valued at the amount posted for that charge divided by the months of cover it pays for, rounded to the cent.

**Where no charge stands for the opening span and premium has been charged since the supplement took effect** — a month is valued at the premium charged since the supplement took effect divided by the months the policy has been in force.

**Where neither of those holds** — a month is valued at the amount posted for the opening span, taken in full.

### Input, judgement, outcome

> *Input.* A charge of 355.80 stands for the opening span and pays for 3 months of cover.
> *Judgement.* The charge covers more than one month of cover.
> *Outcome.* A month is valued at 355.80 divided by 3, rounded to the cent, being 118.60.

> *Input.* No charge stands for the opening span; premium of 240.00 has been charged since the supplement took effect and the policy has been in force 2 months.
> *Judgement.* No charge stands for the opening span and premium has been charged since it took effect.
> *Outcome.* A month is valued at 240.00 divided by 2, being 120.00.

> *Input.* One charge of 112.40 stands for the opening span and pays for 1 month of cover.
> *Judgement.* The charge does not cover more than one month of cover, and a charge does stand for the span.
> *Outcome.* A month is valued at the amount posted for the opening span taken in full, being 112.40.

The divisor in the first case is the months of cover that charge pays for; the divisor in the second is the months the policy has been in force. The two are different quantities and are never exchanged for one another.
